articleTitle: Terapia Transdérmica para el tratamiento de Hipomagnesemia
abstract: Este trabajo presenta una propuesta de innovación y mejora en cuanto al manejo del tratamiento de pacientes diagnosticados con hipomagnesemia, buscando optar por técnicas poco o nada invasivas para el individuo sometido. Relevancia Clínica— Hoy en día contamos con limitadas técnicas de tratamientos para pacientes con este tipo de padecimiento, por lo que este escrito puede contribuir a la expansión o mejora de tratamientos vigentes.

articleTitle: Inteligencia Artificial: En el diagnóstico temprano de Carcinoma Pulmonar
abstract: Este documento abordará temas de Inteligencia Artificial aplicada en el área de Biomédica, específicamente en la detección temprana de carcinoma pulmonar. Relevancia Clínica— Hoy en día existen diversos métodos para detectar el carcinoma pulmonar, sin embargo, todavía existe un gran porcentaje de errores en el diagnóstico de este padecimiento, una excelente opción para solucionar este problema es implementar la Inteligencia Artificial al análisis de Bioimágenes.

articleTitle: Electrohysterography Reveals Differences in the Propagation of Uterine Electrical Dynamics Between Obese and Non-Obese Parturient Women
abstract: This study investigates the variations in the propagation of uterine electrical dynamics between obese and non-obese pregnant women using electrohysterography (EHG). Precisely monitoring uterine activity during pregnancy is crucial for achieving optimal pregnancy outcomes. However, conventional methods lack the capability to assess uterine electrical dynamics accurately. EHG records the electrical activity of myometrial cells through surface electrodes. Our hypothesis posits that obese and non-obese pregnant women demonstrate distinct uterine electrical propagation patterns during labor. In this exploratory study, transabdominal records were obtained from Mexican parturient women, with the Control or Non-Obese group (n=10) comprising women of healthy weight (BMI between 18.5 to 24.9 kg/m2) and the Obesity group (n=10) consisting of obese women (BMI higher than 30 kg/m2). These records were captured using portable equipment designed to measure biopotentials. Vertical and horizontal vectors were generated from multiple electrode-channel of EHG signals and subjected to filtering across various frequency bands, spanning from 0.3 to 5 Hz. Subsequently, mutual information analysis explored nonlinear correlations between vertical and horizontal channels. The results of mutual information analysis revealed differences in the vertical vectors within the frequency range of 2.2 to 3.5 Hz between the Control and Obesity groups. The Obesity group exhibited lower mean mutual information values than the Control group. (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex> =0.0315). Trending levels were also observed in other vertical pairs and frequency bands. Our findings suggest that adipose tissue may influence myometrial electrical signal propagation patterns during labor. Clinical Relevance– The mutual information analysis of EHG signals in multiple bands shows how uterine electrical activity propagation differs among non-obese and obese women, ensuring optimal pregnancies involve precise monitoring during labor. In essence, these results provide valuable insights into the intricate interplay between obesity, the electrophysiological dynamics of uterine activity and the progress of labor.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Evaluation of Bioreactor to Decellularize and Recellularize Human Muscular Arteries
abstract: The typical vascular pathways utilized in many vascular procedures are either from donors or synthetic materials, frequently resulting in issues due to immune system suppression and limited longevity. Tissue engineering presents an innovative approach to produce personalized grafts featuring a natural extracellular matrix populated with recipient cells through the process of decellularization and recellularization. We show a detailed method to perform human iliac artery decellularization by radial flow perfusion; our radial flow bioreactor and their design and parametrization were published in other job. The artery was decellularized by with perfusion and recirculation of 1% of sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) for 7 days, with changes every 24 h. SDS was perfused at 35 mL/min at 25°C. The iliac artery was cleaned in ultrapure water with PBS. Washed again in PBS and preconditioned in endothelial medium and DNase. The decellularized artery with the bioreactor and the UNAM protocol appeared white in contrast to the normal vain. Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and DAPI staining demonstrated the presence of nuclei in normal and in decellularized arteries was better in the UNAM protocol than our bioreactor at same time; but the previous protocol uses 1750 ml of media against 490 ml. Our bioreactor, demonstrated to be an adequate and optimum decellularized system, we need just increase the perfusion time, in addition of providing efficient decellularized vain ready to Recellularize it in the same chamber.

articleTitle: Automatic Estimation of Skin Perfusion Pressure Based on Multi-wavelength Photoplethysmography Data.
abstract: Skin perfusion pressure (SPP) is a helpful test for assessing tissular perfusion in cases such as peripheral vascular disease. It is usually measured using modern imaging techniques, and although there are inexpensive options, these are not employed since they rely on visual inspections. In this work, we propose and evaluate using a plethysmography (PPG) sensor to estimate skin perfusion pressure automatically. Our proposal is a simple methodology based on derivatives and evaluates it using an occlusion and deflation protocol. We employ PPG measurements from three different wavelengths. This initial evaluation is applied to 10 participants who signed an informed consent. The results show that the data from the three wavelengths are highly correlated, and the SPP estimations are similar, with average measurements of 70 ± 8mmHg, 71 ± 7mmHg, and 75 ± 9mmHg for green, red, and infrared wavelengths, respectively. Future work will focus on further validation and the exploration of contactless methods to estimate SPP. Clinical Relevance—We propose an economical, quantitative, objective method for estimating SPP, which could aid physicians in assessing diseases such as peripheral vascular disease and making decisions regarding amputation in severe cases

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation for Lanes in Running Track to Assist Blind Athletes
abstract: This work presents a technological solution to increase the autonomy of blind athletes or with visual disability in their training, using neural networks to segment every lane of the track field in real-time along with a device that captures the video signal in front of the athlete and indicates by vibrations when a curve is approaching or when a deviation from the lane is occurring. The results show great performance in the segmentation of the lanes and the timely indications to the athlete to keep him in the lane.

articleTitle: RehabGame: A Hand Exoskeleton and Video Game Interface for Home Rehabilitation
abstract: Historically, rehabilitation services have been a low priority for many governments, especially those with limited investment in health, resulting in poorly coordinated and underdeveloped services [1]. This is why our project focuses on the creation of a rehabilitation interface with lower long-term cost that can be used from home, this rehabilitation interface consists of a hand exoskeleton, an electromyography module and a video game, this interface will aim to help the individual to achieve the highest level of function, independence and quality of life possible, in addition to motivate the constancy and recurrence of patients to follow the treatment by providing a convenient option at a distance, with a motivating environment that facilitates their participation in rehabilitation. This work shows the design and development process of the prototype created. Clinical Relevance– Its purpose is to facilitate the attainment of the highest level of functionality, independence, and quality of life for individuals. Furthermore, it aims to foster patients' consistency and adherence to treatment by providing a convenient remote option, with a motivating environment to actively engage in their rehabilitation.

articleTitle: Biosensor de ADN basado en bioimpedancia por inducción magnética
abstract: Actualmente los biosensores para la detección de ADN usan métodos basados en marcado y funcionalización lo cual puede alterar las propiedades biológicas o químicas de las muestras. Por ello, se diseñó un prototipo de biosensor para la detección de ADN libre de marcado y funcionalización mediante bioimpedancia por inducción magnética. Relevancia clínica— El biosensor de detección de ADN tiene potencial para la detección de enfermedades genéticas y contribuyendo a revolucionar la práctica médica al proporcionar diagnósticos tempranos y más precisos.

articleTitle: SELFIES RxNet: Empowering Reaction Synthesis Through Symbolic Notations and AI
abstract: We present a Deep Learning generative self-supervised chemical reaction model based on Bidirectional and Auto-Regressive Transformer (BART) architecture. We made a model that is able to generate and predict reactions in SMILES representation to produce valid molecules only.

Author Keywords: Due to the fact that generative models are capable of generating novel data
they can create de novo reactions that could be more efficient and

articleTitle: Exploring the Reconstruction of Electrocardiograms from Photoplethysmograms via Deep Learning
abstract: The aim of this study is to explore the reconstruction of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals from photoplethysmography (PPG) signals, using data from healthy and diseased volunteers. To this aim, we review a novel method based in deep learning to reconstruct ECG signals and test it on two public databases: MIMIC-III and BIDMC. In the MIMICIII database, the system's behavior was analyzed in response to different frequency contents of the ECG (0.5 to 20 Hz, 0.5 to 40 Hz and 0.5 to 60 Hz), as well as variations in window width (1 s, 2 s, 3 s and 4 s). Furthermore, comparative tests were conducted between healthy and diseased volunteers. In the second database, the validation of the method was verified. The average correlation values obtained in MIMIC-III and BIDMC were higher than 0.80, confirming the previous results reported in the literature. In the final analysis, the system behavior using data from patients with pre-existing conditions exhibited inferior performance compared to those who were in good health. Clinical Relevance — It is feasible to reconstruct ECG signals from PPG signals under controlled clinical conditions. However, it is still necessary to continue exploring reconstruction methods as the one employed here exhibited lower performance in patients with preexisting heart diseases than in healthy subjects.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Pharmacological Treatment in Acute Osteo Arthrosis Model by Means of Kinematic Analysis and Pain Threshold
abstract: The proposed study proves the option to have a different treatment displayed on quantitative and qualitative parameters of kinematics and pain tests, by experiments with mice groups during walk and mobility analysis with kinematics parameters and pain sensation using Von Frey filaments in acute osteoarthritis knee (AOAK) model. This would allow us to have enough information to recommend or not recommend a new based treatment that can be compared to another successful treatment for osteoarthritis. Clinical Relevance — Therefore, with this study it is proposed to be able to analyze different compounds from opioids, steroids, and non-steroid anti-inflammatories (NSAIDs) like cannabinoid components, avoiding with that the dependance pathology and renal damage in patients treated with one of this kind of common treatments and thus be able to determine their viability on a in vivo model to recommend their study in instances closer to a clinical model.

articleTitle: Development of a Portable System for the Acquisition of EMG and NIRS Signals
abstract: The development of prosthetic systems is a subject of significant interest among scientists worldwide. Today, highly advanced prostheses can be controlled through the detection of muscle impulses. On the other hand, the use of near-infrared spectroscopy has not been widely employed for this purpose, despite its capability to detect changes in muscle oxygenation levels. This work aims to integrate both signals through a custom-designed instrumentation system capable of detecting both physiological effects in the same muscle. Clinical Relevance—This project presents the development of a portable device capable of superficially measuring muscle contractions through voltage levels and spectroscopy. All of this is aimed at creating a prosthetic control system that is easier to use for amputees and can detect a wider range of movements

articleTitle: Sensor Fault Tolerant Treatment for Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus Patients
abstract: This paper presents a novel data-based fault tolerant treatment strategy to improve life quality of Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus Patients. This approach is based on an inverse optimal neural controller modified to deal with sensor communication faults

articleTitle: Characterization of EEG Signals from Healthy Subjects While Being Stimulated by Heat and Cold
abstract: This research explores gender differences in pain perception by analyzing Electroencephalographic (EEG) signals. The study involves 10 healthy subjects and includes induction of thermal sensations, and analysis of bandpower changes before and after stimuli. According to the results, alpha-bandpower is higher when the subjects feel pain with heat than with cold. Clinical Relevance– This work might be considered as an approach to find a pain threshold in men and women.

articleTitle: Towards Obstructive Sleep Apnea Prediction through the Application of Machine Learning Techniques on Biometric Data
abstract: Machine learning techniques have found utility as predictive tools in diagnosing Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA). It has been observed that integrating specific types of data improves the accuracy of OSA severity prediction. The objective of this research is to create a reliable model for predicting OSA, using machine learning techniques on combined biometric data. Clinical Relevance — OSA is a condition associated with neurological, cardiovascular and metabolic problems. Given that the conventional diagnostic method is slow, expensive and invasive, the demand for quicker, more cost-effective and minimally invasive alternatives remains

articleTitle: Obtaining Descriptors Related to Sperm Quality for Automatic Filtering in ICSI
abstract: In ICSI the sperm selection is based on a qualitative evaluation of dozens of sperms in motion simultaneously, which makes it difficult to find the most appropriate. In this work we seek to generate descriptors related to the quality of the sperm, using computer vision to obtain signals from the sperm movement and using signal analysis techniques to obtain patterns that can correlate with a quality assessment made by an embryologist. Clinical Relevance — This can help embryologists to make a more objective decision in the selection process of spermatozoa in ICSI and improve the success rate of the technique.

articleTitle: Enhancing Electrical Cochlear Response Quality in Cochlear Implant Apical Electrodes Using Empirical Mode Decomposition
abstract: The auditory evoked potential, recorded on the scalp while an implanted subject uses their device in everyday mode, is called the Electrical Cochlear Response (ECR). The waveform and amplitude of this potential vary with sound stimulus intensity and frequency, thus containing useful information about hearing provided by Cochlear Implant (CI). Depending on the CI design criterion, the electrical current stimulation rate in apical electrodes may be higher than in middle and basal electrodes. A high stimulation rate produces an electrical artifact interfering with ECR detection and measuring in apical electrodes. In this paper, we compare two methods based on Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) to select and remove the electrical artifact produced in the apical electrodes due to a high current stimulation rate. The performance of both methods was evaluated using ECR signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and waveform quality after artifact removal. Both methods generally had similar performance with a significant SNR improvement. However, only one of them preserves ECR waveform across electrodes. Clinical Relevance—Clinical judgment about hearing provided by Cochlear Implants to the patient is based on ECR detection and latency and peak amplitude measure in each stimulation electrode; hence, SNR and waveform quality improvement of ECR allows clinicians to determine these features better

articleTitle: EEG Frontal Alpha Asymmetry analysis with binaural music for anxiety reduction
abstract: In this article the use of binaural music (8D music) for anxiety reduction is explored. Binaural music has been present since 1983 but it has resurfaced in recent years allowing people to listen to it in different music streaming platforms such as Spotify. In this research, a comparison between regular music and binaural music has been made. Showing the differences in the brain of both men and women while using a known biomarker known as alpha asymmetry comparing the left side of the brain with the right side. Relaxation is achieved in all participants, but binaural music seems to be more efficient in men than women. Clinical Relevance—This study shows a different approach to anxiety reduction using binaural music. In here, binaural music appears to be more relaxing in men than women

articleTitle: Diurnal EEG Alterations in Obstructive Sleep Apnea Hypopnea Syndrome and Hypercapnia
abstract: Characterized as a prevalent sleep disorder, Obstructive Sleep Apnea Hypopnea Syndrome (OSAHS) is linked to cognitive deficits that impact attention, memory, learning, and executive functions. OSAHS can lead to elevated levels of carbon dioxide (CO2) in the blood, a condition known as Hypercapnia, which further contributes to cognitive impairment and results in slower EEG activity measured in polysomnography studies. In this study, we explore changes on EEG from recordings during a Stroop test realization on awake subjects to evidence effects of bad sleep hygiene. We compared OSAHS patients (with and without Hypercapnia) to healthy individuals, aiming to understand changes on EEG patterns with severity of OSAHS condition. Simultaneously, we evaluate patients identification between OSAHS patients and a Control group by using features extracted from EEG band power analysis. Assessment of identification was conducted using various algorithms; however, the support vector machine (SVM) stands out, achieving the best performance with an Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) of 0.9031 and an accuracy (ACC) of 0.7933. Findings show that changes on EEG waves are present even on patient's vigil that could be an indicator of OSAHS impact. An opens possibility to use this features as biomarkers for OSAHS evaluation obtained during patient wakeful time and not only in polysomnography studies.

articleTitle: Intelligent Algorithms for On-Line Anomaly Detection in Photoplethysmography Signals
abstract: Photoplethysmography signals (PPG) can produce a wide variety of biological information that can be useful for the detection and diagnosis of heart disease. These signals are produced by photoplethysmography sensors that are typically found in devices such as a vital signs monitor or pulse oximeter. The information produced is susceptible to common artifacts (e.g., sensor movements, poor skin contact) that can cause alerts in monitoring devices and lead to confusion in providing treatment or diagnosis. The present work deals with intelligent algorithms for on-line detection of anomalies that may occur in photoplethysmography signals and that can help to improve diagnostics where this technology is used.

articleTitle: Continuous Mental State Estimation Using EEG Band Power Time Series Predictions for BCI Control
abstract: Long Short-Term Memory network (LSTM) can be used as a prediction model that reproduces time series dynamics based on training data. Here, LSTM was used to predict changes on EEG band power time series (BPts) trained with data from two different mental tasks, assuming that BPts dynamics should differ between those two tasks. Prediction error was used as a single feature to continuously identify mental state. AUROC values were calculated, achieving 0.672 ± 0.027 on f3 band as best result. Clinical relevance - Band power time series (BPts) have been used to explore dynamics of the autonomic branches, and also as a descriptor of their functional integrity. This work explores if such dynamics change by subject intention or specific task execution. This was a first attempt at using BPts as BCI control signals, but analysis shows that their dynamics are more related to intrinsic neural modulation. If the former is true, then BPts could be explored as biomarkers of autonomic alterations.

articleTitle: An Approach to Cellular Diversity in the Human Brain
abstract: Over history, the brain has been studied from different perspectives, some trying to uncover the structural and informative essential components that live in each region along the brain. However, some issues lack an appropriate definition, like the neuron type concept itself, and therefore, the cell distribution along the brain remains unclear. This work gives a cellular diversity description inferring in silico the fractions of cell types known along the human brain.

articleTitle: Toward a Brain-Controlled Electric Wheelchair Based on Steady State Visual Evoked Potentials
abstract: Severe motor disabilities can significantly impact people's quality of life, impeding their mobility and independence in daily activities. While electric wheelchairs often provide a solution to enhance mobility, these are hard to control for people with these disabilities. In this context, EEG-based brain-computer interfaces (BCI) offer a promising avenue for controlling assistive devices. BCls allow users to interact with their environment by detecting and analyzing brain-generated electrical signals. This study focuses on designing and implementing a modular control system for an electric wheelchair with brain signals.

articleTitle: Improving Nonlinearity Parameter Imaging Using Compounding
abstract: Ultrasound is an imaging modality widely used for clinical applications such as disease diagnosing and tissue characterization. The quality of ultrasound images is generally restricted by speckle noise, which degrades the quality of not only conventional ultrasonographic imaging but also novel quantitative ultrasound techniques. In this work, we used both frequency and spatial plane wave compounding to improve the quality of nonlinearity parameter (B/A) imaging. In silico backscattered echo data were acquired by simulating a linear array transducer and a media excited with a 5 MHz pulse at two excitation peak pressures, 80 kPa and 400 kPa. A nonuniform nonlinear simulated media was composed of an 18-mm diameter circular inclusion (with B/A=11) in an otherwise uniform background (with B/A = 6). Using plane wave compounding with 21 plane waves allowed reducing the standard deviation of the resulting B/A images by a factor of 2 when compared to a single plane wave transmission sequence. This can be further improved to a threefold reduction when plane wave compounding is combined with frequency compounding. The results show how spatial plane wave and frequency compounding methods improve contrast and background smoothing when the B/A is estimated. Clinical Relevance– Ultrasonic tissue characterization could be improved by the estimation of the nonlinearity parameter (B/A), a source of contrast in ultrasonic imaging, with a novel pulse-echo approach called the depletion method. However, B/A images suffer from low signal-to-noise ratios. Using a combination of spatial and frequential compounding, the quality of B/A images using a depletion method is significantly improved, with potential to be used in commonly available clinical scanners.

articleTitle: Towards Biosignals Analysis for the Automatic Assessment of Upper Limb Impairment
abstract: To restore lost functions resulting from strokes, a thorough assessment of the impairments is crucial. The objective of this work is to assess upper limb impairment by using two different biosignals.

articleTitle: Development of a Raspberry Pi-Based Circuit to Detect Drowsiness in Drivers and Prevent Traffic Accidents
abstract: Drowsiness is one of the main causes of traffic accidents. This work presents a Raspberry Pi 4-based drowsiness detection system that uses closed eyes detection to identify drowsy drivers. The system uses a camera module to capture images of the driver's face and then applies the Haar cascade algorithm to detect if the driver's eyes are closed for more than a certain amount of time, in case of exceeding that time, the system will sound an alarm to alert the driver, and with this, it can prevent accidents by promptly alerting the driver if they have fallen asleep. Furthermore, it is highlighted that the device does not pose a visual obstruction or cause any discomfort due to its size and operation.

articleTitle: Electroencephalographic Response to a Casual Video Game Played on Stress and Anxiety Patients: A Study of Beta/Alpha and Theta/Beta Ratios
abstract: The increasing prevalence of mental disorders in recent years has prompted the exploration of alternative approaches to alleviate their symptoms. This paper presents an analysis of electroencephalographic (EEG) signals, conducted on stressed and anxious participants to investigate the potential benefits of using a casual video game (CVG) as a therapeutic intervention. The study focuses on assessing the Beta/Alpha Ratio (BAR) and Theta/Beta Ratio (THBR) to demonstrate the well-being effects of employing CVGs. The analysis indicates that after CVG usage, participants exhibited a BAR of less than 1.13 and a THBR higher than 0.72, suggesting positive outcomes in symptom mitigation. Clinical Relevance—This is a result to demonstrate CVGs can be used as a potential tool to improve the health in patients with mental disorders

articleTitle: Estimation of Tissue Perfusion Parameters with Multispectral Images and Machine Learning Regression Models
abstract: The study investigated various regression strategies to estimate perfusion characteristic maps during an arterial occlusion protocol using multispectral images. The proposed approach involves a preliminary nonlinear unmixing stage utilizing the Nonlinear Extended Blind End-Members and Abundance Extraction (NEBEAE) method for feature extraction. Subsequently, machine learning regression models are employed to estimate perfusion characteristics, specifically the change in oxygenated hemoglobin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Delta HbO_{2})$</tex>. As a reference, punctual estimation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta HbO_{2}$</tex> via a photoplethysmography (PPG) signal was included. The regression results demonstrated determination coefficients reaching up to 0.993 and normalized errors as low as 0.042. The nonlinear unmixing stage utilized only three end-members to generate precise <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta HbO_{2}$</tex> maps. This not only reduces the information needed for estimation but also minimizes spectral decomposition and processing time. Consequently, the results suggest the potential for real-time application in future research.

articleTitle: Computational Method for Tridimensional Reconstruction of Human Blastocysts
abstract: The success of in vitro fertilization (IVF) is intricately linked to the precise selection of viable blastocysts. However, the limitations in relying solely on 2D microscope images to observe blastocysts have encouraged the pursuit of alternative methodologies. In response to this and the few proposals to obtain 3D models of the blastulas, we develop a computational algorithm for reconstructing 3D models of human blastocysts from 2D images previously acquired through bright-field microscopy. This 3D model holds the potential to enhance the blastula selection by facilitating improved visual morphology, potentially unearthing relevant insights into their distinctive features and attributes.

Author Keywords: Addressing the limitations of current 2D-based blastocyst and by providing embryologists with 3D (A) models showcasing a wider range of morphological features
this innovation could enhance the accuracy of blastocyst assessment. Ultimately
this could lead to improve IVF outcomes by enabling the selection of higher quality embryos
consequently increasing the chances of successful pregnancies

articleTitle: Programa de Mentoría Virtual en Ingeniería Biomédica: Un Enfoque Transformador para la Educación STEM en Perú
abstract: In Peru, the supply of academic programmes in biomedical engineering is limited, which places the country at a disadvantage with respect to global and regional development. In response to this need, students at the Universidad Nacional Mayor de San Marcos created the Biomentoring Program in 2021 to introduce high school students to biomedical engineering and foster their interest in this constantly evolving discipline. The methodology was based on the project-based learning approach, cooperative and collaborative learning, and educational gamification. They worked in collaborative groups of secondary school students, called Mentees, together with university students and professionals, called Biomentors. As a result, in 2021, this initiative provided the opportunity for 34 Biomentores and more than 100 Mentees from various regions of Peru to improve their knowledge, skills and innovation capacity in STEM and Biomedical Engineering.

articleTitle: Description of Open- and Closed-Loop Cardiovascular and Cardiorespiratory Interactions at 11 – 14 weeks' gestation in Pregnancies that Subsequently Developed Preeclampsia
abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) affects 3-8% of all pregnancies and causes severe outcomes for the mother and offspring during and years after pregnancy. Clinical manifestation of PE starts in the 2nd - 3rd trimester, but some pregnant may be asymptomatic. Thus, to have proper management of PE and reduce severe maternal/fetal complications, early detection and prediction of PE is necessary, and remains challenging due to unknown PE origin and its heterogeneity. This study aims to explore mechanisms involving heart rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, and respiration in the first trimester of pregnancy, before clinical manifestation of PE. We studied a group of 23 Mexican first-trimester pregnant women who subsequently developed PE, a control group of 23 normotensive women throughout pregnancy, and a control group of normotensive pregnant without comorbidities. Preliminary results from this study showed increased hemodynamic indices in women that subsequently developed PE and no differences between studied groups in the baroreflex sensitivity open-loop assessment; meanwhile, some closed-loop interactions were different among the normotensive groups, which could be comorbidities-related. Moreover, we observed differences in the correlation of interaction indices with hemodynamic ones among the studied groups, having PE correlation with mean arterial pressure rather than pulse wave velocity. Clinical Relevance– This study shows differences in the closed-loop cardiovascular and cardiorespiratory interaction indices previous to the clinical manifestation of preeclampsia.

articleTitle: Machine Learning and Data Analysis in the Prevention of Complications Derived from Diabetes
abstract: Diabetes is a metabolic disease of particular concern in México. Since Mexico has one of the highest rates of diabetes prevalence in the world, it is estimated that around 13-15% of Mexico's population has diabetes. This research establishes the precise relationship between patient habits and the development of complications associated with this pathology through machine learning techniques and data analysis. The obtained results provide a precise understanding of how certain habits of diabetic patients are directly linked to the development of complications such as heart attacks, vision loss, and amputations, among others.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Relationship between Gene Expression and Functional Connectivity using Multi-Scale Analysis
abstract: Extracting whole-brain gene expression (GE) data with high resolution i.e., cell-level, is technically challenging. As an alternative, neuroimaging is more accessible and allows a macroscopic study of the whole brain. This study aims to explore how GE is related to resting-state functional connectivity (FC) patterns.

Author Keywords: The relationship between GE and FC
would allow get a reliable picture of brain functioning and the pathologies associated with its malfunctioning

articleTitle: A Simulation Study to Evaluate Constraints for Nonlinearity Parameter Estimation Using the Depletion Method
abstract: The acoustic nonlinearity parameter (B/A) can assess changes in structure and identify tissue characteristics. Its accurate estimation is critical for correct ultrasound imaging and diagnosis, particularly in liver diseases. Recently, a pulseecho B/A estimation method has been developed based on the quantification of a term called the depletion of the fundamental band, using a dual-energy approach and a reference phantom. This method is accurate even though the medium and reference phantom have different attenuation coefficients. Through a methodology based on computer simulations of sample and reference phantom media, this study aims to identify constraints in the estimation of the B/A using the depletion method to measure the influence of factors such as the low excitation pressure, the scaling factor between low and high pressures, and the attenuation mismatch between reference phantom media and sample. The use of computer models of pulse-echo ultrasound provided a controlled environment to investigate the impact of these variables on the B/A estimation process. The results show that cases using moderate scaling factors (5-10) and moderate initial pressures (40-400 kPa) resulted in mean and standard deviation percentage error values usually below 10%, even in the case of 33% attenuation mismatch. Clinical Relevance—Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a type of steatosis that affects individuals who consume little or no alcohol. The overall prevalence of NAFLD worldwide was estimated to be 32.4%. An innovative approach for NAFLD early diagnosis is the use of the B/A that can be addressed with a better understanding of constraints of the recently proposed depletion method

articleTitle: Towards Fibrotic Tissue Automatic Estimation in Computer Tomography Interstitial Lung Disease
abstract: This work presents an implementation of lung segmentation using U-net as a part of a chain process in detecting radiological findings and estimating fibrosis volume applied in computer tomography. Clinical Relevance — This implementation establishes an automatic tool that helps in the diagnosis and clinical monitoring of patients with interstitial lung disease.

articleTitle: Development of an Artificial Intelligence System Based on the Windkessel Model for Arterial Hypertension Identification
abstract: This paper presents an artificial intelligence (AI) system utilizing the Windkessel model for hypertension modeling. By analyzing blood pressure data with machine learning algorithms, the system achieves accurate estimations. The proposed approach enhances diagnosis, aiding healthcare professionals in informed decision-making, ultimately improving patient outcomes and reducing cardiovascular risks. Clinical Relevance—A system of artificial intelligence (AI) to model of arterial hypertension provides early diagnosis, improves accuracy, supports clinical decisions and personalizes treatment. In order to improve the prevention of complications and enhances patients' life quality

articleTitle: Sensor Placement for Perfusion Parameters Estimation in Feet
abstract: There is no consensus on where perfusion parameters should be measured using plethysmography sensors in the lower limb. In this work, we evaluate the correlation between sensors located in four different positions according to the angiosome model. We evaluated an occlusion protocol to induce changes in the levels of oxygenated and deoxygenated hemoglobin. We gathered data from 16 healthy participants. We found a strong Pearson correlation (r>0.8) between a sensor located in the heel and the measurements from the medial dorsal and hallux toe. The results could be used to assess the best sensor placement in cases where the location of the sensor is restricted.

articleTitle: Segmentation of Sperm Flagellum Using a Temporal Local Motion Estimation
abstract: Sperm flagellum is often poorly visible and difficult to detect while being useful in research and IVF treatments. A pixel-wise temporal analysis is used to estimate motion and processed to obtain a segmentation of the flagellum. 83% of the length of the flagellum is successfully segmented on average.

Author Keywords: This can improve the scope of analysis CASA system utilize and help make a more objective decision in the selection process of spermatozoa in ICSI

articleTitle: El Dolor de Miembro Fantasma: Exploración de la Neurorrehabilitación Utilizando Realidad Virtual y Señales Eléctricas: Contreras Gonzalez Jose
abstract: Resumen− El Dolor de Miembro Fantasma (DMF) en amputados plantea preguntas sobre la relación entre el dolor y las conexiones neuronales. La realidad virtual y la neurorrehabilitación se proponen como soluciones, manipulando señales eléctricas para controlar prótesis y esclarecer la percepción del movimiento. Relevancia Clínica−El análisis de señales para el DMF puede ser de gran ayuda para crear prótesis que sean controladas únicamente con el pensamiento, con el fin de poder realizar movimientos más complejos.

articleTitle: Gait Event Detection Algorithm for Spastic Cerebral Palsy
abstract: Existing kinematic algorithms for detecting initial contact (IC) and toe-off (TO) often lack precision in clinical applications. This study presents an algorithm that demonstrates robustness in detecting gait events in pathological data, effectively addressing various gait patterns and algorithms. Clinical Relevance—In commercial motion analysis systems, the onset of step definition is currently performed manually by specialists. Our algorithm addresses the deficiency in precision for pathological gait patterns and algorithms

articleTitle: Análisis de Datos COVID-19 Utilizando Algoritmos de Inteligencia Artificial
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has markedly catalyzed the advancement of innovative tools. With the aim of crafting resilient predictive models, an extensive training process has been executed to anticipate the risk of mortality or survival associated with the categories of moderate/severe hospitalization and critical patient cases. Clinical Relevance—Metabolites can play a significant role in mitigating the complications associated with COVID-19 and can also contribute to a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms involved in the development of prolonged symptoms caused by SARS-CoV-2 infection

articleTitle: Evaluation of Interaction Between DEHP Metabolites with Different Cytochromes P450 Families Through Molecular Docking
abstract: This research contributes to the development of therapeutic agents based on the analysis of cytochrome families p450 against the DEHP plasticizer molecule and its metabolite MEHP. To characterize the molecular interaction, we computationally implemented molecular docking as a binding prediction technique, considering measurement and selection parameters to evaluate the inhibition in the enzymatic activity. Clinical Relevance—Evaluating the interaction of different P450 cytochromes against DEHP and its metabolites in the organism allows progress in the development of specific therapeutic agents against inhibition in enzymatic activity

articleTitle: ECG Features Extraction to Semiautomatic Detection of Atrial Fibrillation
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are heart abnormalities that gradually lead to decreased oxygen supply to all body's vital parts, affecting other organs such as the brain and lungs due to the heart's poor functioning. While specialists diagnose these diseases using ECG waveforms and their physical properties, the sporadic nature of cardiac events often results in delayed detection. Numerous scientists have focused on digital signal processing of ECG to facilitate semi-automatic diagnosis. This paper introduces an algorithm that blends wavelet transform with digital filtering techniques to identify features indicative of atrial fibrillation. Clinical Relevance— Our algorithm paves the way for a semiautomatic cardiac diagnostic tool for emergency settings, enabling rapid 10-second signal analyses without the need for expert visual assessment, reducing error chances.

articleTitle: Variation of Cellular Proportions During Homeostasis and Regeneration of Ambystoma Mexicanum Brain Throughout its Life Cycle
abstract: This study focused on analyzing cell proportions in the homeostasis (un-injured) and regeneration (injured) of Axolotl's (Ambystoma mexicanum) brain during its life cycle using single-nuclei (snRNA-seq) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data. By applying machine learning tools (CIBERSORTx), we expect to estimate cell proportions at both stages, providing detailed insight into proportional changes and their influence on regeneration.

Author Keywords: Integrating our findings into computational models offers potential for enhanced strategies in regenerative medicine
predicting how interventions might modulate tissue recovery. This not only advances our understanding of regeneration but also strengthens treatment efficacy in biomedicine

articleTitle: Strategy for Validation of the Optimal Temperature of the Enzyme-Substrate Complex by Molecular Dynamics Simulation
abstract: Molecular dynamics simulations provide an understanding of molecular interactions and give us a measure of the affinity as a function of environmental variables such as temperature. The simulation provides us with information about the number of hydrogen bonds formed, RMSD and potential energy. The study aims to compare the affinity of the Phytoene-β-carotene synthase - geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate complex by varying temperatures and allows us to validate the optimal value for the enzymatic reaction.

articleTitle: Spatial Blind Source Separation for an Age Neuroimaging Analysis
abstract: As individuals age, the brain undergoes structural, functional and connectivity changes. Brain activity and anatomy do not always correspond, then evolving differently. In this regard, Independent Component Analysis (ICA) for brain parcellation proves advantageous in studying brain function with a comprehensive and flexible approach that spans across all stages of life. We proposed a method based on ICA that estimates coherent anatomical networks based on functional connectivity patterns. Clinical Relevance—The analysis of brain function across various age groups will aid in the investigation of conditions or pathologies related to alterations in functional connectivity, such as autism spectrum disorder, Alzheimer´s disease, major depressive disorder and epilepsy

articleTitle: Proof-of-Concept Study of Image-Generating AIs As a Tool for Graphical Abstracts
abstract: Graphical abstracts are a visual representation of the abstract, to gain visibility and succinctly display the study findings. To design graphical abstract for scientific articles through image-generating AIs, we carried out a proof-of-concept study using abstracts as prompts. With prompt engineering, partial abstract parts and full abstract yielded similar images. We observe that AI's still do not reach the ability to generate a coherent image with abstract discourse, but lead to a big creative jump to build one. This bias resulted from keywords AIs attention and a non-homogeneous guideline to picture a graphical abstract over merely workflow illustrations. Relevance— To write prompts to generate graphical abstracts allowing us to use image-generating AIs as we currently work with other AIs as translators, search engines or even chats. Also to challenge current graphical abstract beyond a workflow diagram towards an abstract but illustrative picture of the article content.

articleTitle: Estimating the QT Interval from the Features Analysis of BCG and PCG signals
abstract: QT interval has clinical relevance since it is linked to ventricular arrhythmias and sudden death. Some drugs, systemic diseases, and genetics can modify it. Specialists usually obtain it manually from digital or printed electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings, which is a cumbersome task. For this reason, some algorithms have been proposed to make this diagnostic procedure efficient, faster, and cheaper. However, these approaches have limitations because a huge quantity of data and 12-lead ECG are required for classification methods. In this work, it is proposed to use other physiological signals with feasible acquisition procedures such as ballistocardiogram (BCG) and phonocardiogram (PCG) to extract information that could be related to QT interval or that could help to detect the T-wave end. This feature is a challenging one due to masking by U wave or by drifts in the isoelectric line. Two intervals were proposed here to correlate them with the QT interval: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> wave from ECG to K wave from BCG and H wave from BCG to S2 from PCG. The correlation coefficient between QT and Q-K intervals was 0.569, while the QT and H-S2 correlation was 0.653. Additionally, R2 values of 0.32 and 0.42 for the relationship between (QT, Q-K) and (QT, H-S2) were found. Bland Altman plots compared the proposed intervals with the QT interval where the 95% of the data fell within the agreement limits. These results are promising since both signals, BCG and PCG, could be used in a non-clinical setting in an easy way to help in the detection of QT interval. Clinical Relevance– QT prolongation is related to cardiovascular diseases, then the efforts to detect it effectively can have a health impact. BCG and PCG signals could provide additional information to identify the T-wave end and the overall QT interval.

articleTitle: Assessment of an Automated Wheezing Respiratory Cycle Identification Based on CNN and Classical and High-Resolution Time-Frequency Representations
abstract: Respiratory sounds (RS) provide relevant information that helps diagnose pathologies. Some common continuous adventitious RS are wheezes, present in diseases such as asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). In recent decades, efforts have been made to automatically detect wheezes in RS, e.g., by classical time-frequency (TF) representations such as the spectrogram, which allows the visualization of instantaneous changes in frequency over time. However, due to the characteristics and limitations of the previously used TF representations, the detection of wheezes with these techniques still offers areas of opportunity. In this work, we propose to perform the classification of normal RS cycles and RS cycles containing wheezes using two TF methods: (1) Spectrogram (SP) and (2) Hilbert-Huang Spectrum (HHS), as input to a pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN), the GoogleNet. The proposed method was evaluated on the ICBHI Challenge 2017 database, using 575 wheezing respiratory cycles from 45 patients and 575 normal cycles from 44 subjects. The best experimental result achieved a specificity of 0.883, precision of 0.880, and accuracy of 0.872 for the validation set using SP method. Comparing this performance with those reported in the literature, it was found that the classification results obtained are at least comparable to those reported in most state-of-the-art works.

articleTitle: Ensemble of Artificial Intelligence Classifiers for In-Vivo Identification of Glioblastoma Tumours Using Hyperspectral Images
abstract: TThis study introduces a classification methodology designed for the analysis of in-vivo hyperspectral brain images, aimed at the precise identification of affected regions by glioblastoma tumor. Glioblastoma, known for its aggressive nature and diffuse pattern, poses challenges for accurate intraoperative identification. In fact, current identification procedures rely on intraoperative neuronavigation, which is not accurate, neurosurgeon criteria, which can be subjective, and intraoperative histopathology, which is a time-consuming task. As a result, a two-step approach is proposed to classify hyperspectral in-vivo brain images, which involves non-linear spectral unmixing followed by ensembles of well-know artificial intelligence classification algorithms. Two distinct approaches, namely intra and inter-patient, were utilized for end-member extraction, training, and evaluation of the artificial intelligence classifiers. First, the end-members estimation was approached by a supervised perspective with labeled pixels in the HS images. The corresponding abundances and nonlinear interaction levels obtained from non-linear spectral unmixing were used as features for classification. Our experimental results indicate that the intra-patient approach achieved satisfactory performance using a single classification algorithm. However, in the inter-patient approach, the ensemble technique emerged as the preferred choice by its improved performance. In this way, our results highlight the importance of leveraging ensemble methods when labeled data is limited.

articleTitle: Tuning of a Control Scheme for an Exoskeleton Using Swarm Intelligence
abstract: Neuromuscular conditions affecting the lower extremities have a significant global incidence, which often results in difficulty with everyday tasks such as walking. The development of exoskeletons for rehabilitation or support in walking activities can be of great help to people with mobility problems. This paper discusses a method to properly estimate the gains of a motion controller that calculates input torque at the joints of a 3-degree-of-freedom (DOF) exoskeleton through tracking error minimization. It is hypothesized that using optimization methods to derive numerical values for the controller's parameters, such as collective intelligence algorithms, could reduce tracking errors within a multi-joint system such as an exoskeleton. Clinical Relevance - Research into exoskeletons is emerging as a potential means of enhancing the quality of life for individuals afflicted by neuromuscular conditions that impact their lower limbs.

articleTitle: Classification of Parkinson Tremor Using Accelerometer Signals and Long Short-Term Memory Network
abstract: Tremor is the most characteristic symptom of Parkinson's disease (PD), making its precise differentiation from other tremors crucial for successful diagnosis and subsequently effective treatment. This study presents a methodology for differentiation between patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) and healthy subjects (HS) based on accelerometer (ACC) signals. Information from both upper extremities, acquired simultaneously through a wireless system, is used in order to employ a less complex architecture for classification by means of a variation of a recurrent neural network (RNN), using as input ACC time series signals. An accuracy and precision of 88% were achieved using the “Finger-Nose” maneuver, which allows for better differentiation between groups. Clinical Relevance– The use of automated classification systems represents a potential supportive tool in diagnosis for clinical experts, especially during the early stages of PD, aiming to reduce misdiagnosis. On the other hand, employing deep learning techniques also enables the extraction of information not perceived by humans, which could enhance diagnostic sensitivity, specificity, and efficiency, as well as reduce diagnosis time.

articleTitle: Unraveling GABA-Related Metabolic Pathways in Diverse Bifidobacterium Species
abstract: The microbiota exerts a significant influence on health and physiology through intricate interactions with hosts. This study examines the GABA-associated metabolic pathways in various Bifidobacterium species across host taxa, utilizing the KEGG pathway database. Our findings suggest that Bifidobacterium species associated with insects are distinct from those linked to mammals. Clinical Relevance– This research enhances understanding of GABA-associated pathways in Bifidobacterium, thus contributing to our comprehension of microbiota-host interactions and how these can be beneficial for overall health.

articleTitle: Desarrollo De Algoritmo De Diagnóstico Para Aneurismas Saculares Mediante El Procesamiento De Angiotomografias Computarizadas
abstract: This paper aims to discuss the treatment of cerebral aneurysms by employing mathematical techniques to process medical images. The goal is to develop medical software to segment, reconstruct, and measure the lesions examined in this study. This tool will aid in manipulating information, enabling medical professionals to establish diagnoses and treatments for aneurysms at an intermediate level of care.

articleTitle: Increase the Positive Results for AI Zero-Shot Medical Diagnosis
abstract: AI Zero-Shot Medical Diagnosis is currently in an unreliable stage. The creation of more sophisticated AI through fine-tuning opens up the possibility of AI becoming a valuable assistant to medical specialists. Clinical Relevance This establishes a way to increase the true positive results achieved by AI for medical diagnosis and analyzes the possibility of an AI assistant.

articleTitle: Discrimination of Brain States in Go/NoGo Tasks Through Frequency Features in EEG Signals
abstract: Cognitive processes are marked by their dynamic nature, manifesting through varied brain states. In this study, we discriminate electroencephalographic activity between brain states associated with Go/NoGo cognitive tasks using frequency features, which shows the feasibility of explaining brain transition in cognitive processes. Clinical Relevance—Understanding the variability of brain states in cognitive tasks is essential for unraveling the functioning of cognitive processes

articleTitle: Simulación del espectro Raman del Biomarcador N-Óxido de trimetilamina mediante espectroscopia Raman
abstract: Mostramos las frecuencias Raman del biomarcador N-óxido de trimetilamina (TMAO), con el objetivo de comparar el espectro experimental de la sustancia pura y el obtenido mediante software de química cuántica computacional GAUSSIAN ®, a partir de las optimizaciones con mecanismos moleculares Universal Force Field (UFF) y Merck Molecular Force Field 94 (MMFF94), en combinación con las funcionales de Hartree Fock (HF) y la Teoría Funcional de la Densidad (TFD), siendo Becke Lee Yang Parr (B3LYP) el principal funcional híbrido para la obtención de frecuencias Raman aproximadas a los resultados experimentales. Relevancia Clínica— El TMAO es un osmolito que se puede sintetizar a partir de varios precursores, la cantidad presente en el organismo depende de la dieta y la micro flora intestinal. En recientes años se ha identificado que la presencia de altas concentraciones del biomarcador en tejidos biológicos se asocia con diversas enfermedades crónico degenerativas, como hipertensión, síndrome metabólico, diabetes tipo II y eventos cardiovasculares graves. [1]

articleTitle: CT-Based Segmentation and Measurement of Lumbar Segments for Surgical Planning Using Deep Learning
abstract: Problems in the lumbar spine are one of the most disabling issues in the working age population, producing pain, changes in posture or neurological damage. Lumbar fusion surgery with pedicle screws fixation is the most used surgical procedure to treat these types of conditions, such as herniated discs, or spondylolisthesis. Pedicle measurement and segmentation of the lumbar spine, based on CT, are techniques used to plan the surgery effectively, however, these tasks can be complex and time consuming if done manually. Taking this into account, deep learning emerges as a potential solution, as it could effectively automate the measurement and segmentation process. This paper proposes a method that involves a 3D U-Net for segmentation and classification of lumbar segments (vertebrae, pedicles, laminae and apophyses) and autoencoders to extract features from unlabeled images. Measurements are performed thanks to pedicle segmentation, having an approach based on the voxel size obtained in the metadata of each image. This network was trained and validated using a new database from the Hospital Civil de Guadalajara. This method obtained results of 0.0052 and 0.0125 in the MSE and MAE loss function when evaluating the autoencoder, respectively, and 0.0657, 0.9738 and 0.9642 in the Categorical Cross-Entropy, Dice coefficient and IoU index when evaluating 3D U-Net respectively, thus demonstrating that this model is consistent and generalizable, allowing it to measure pedicle segments of new data. Clinical Relevance– This establishes that the use of deep learning algorithms for automatic measurement and classification of lumbar segments has significant clinical relevance as it is very close to matching the accuracy of measurements made by neurosurgeons.

articleTitle: A Novel Feature Extraction Method for Classifying EEG Signals of two types of Reading: Normal Reading and Task-Specific Reading
abstract: Educational contents are designed without considering the students skills and interests. Usually, this scheme provokes a gap between the contents level and the students learning, which impacts in the emotional and stress level of the students. In this scenario, an automatic system to consider the special need of the students is required. For this reason, we develop a first step focused to implement a novel system called neurotutor, which would adapt the contents for each subject. Specifically, this step consists in assessing the differences in EEG signals recorded during two reading tasks: normal reading and task specific reading. Aiming to approach this issue, we propose a novel feature extraction method based on characteristics derived from CWT. This method outperformed the previous work and allowed save computational time consumptions. As a future study, we must investigate if these outcomes can be kept increasing the number of subjects, and considering additional tasks involved during learning processes. Clinical Relevance — A first step targeted to implement an EEG-based neurotutor is presented. This automatic system would help to reduce the student's stress during the process of learning.

articleTitle: Neural Network-Based Intelligent System for Glucose Spike Prediction and Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Risk Assessment
abstract: Machine learning algorithms have revolutionized the management of clinical data to prevent Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM). This paper performs an exploratory study of the relationship between several risk factors, including visceral fat percentage (VF), sedentary lifestyle (SL), sleep hours, adherence to the diet, genetic predisposition (GP), sex, body mass index (BMI), fasting plasma glucose levels (FPG), waist circumference (WC), low dietary fiber intake (LDFI), high carbohydrate intake (HCI), and sleep hygiene, with the development of T2DM. For it, a chi-square statistical tool was used to discern the significance of these features concerning T2DM incidence; among these, VF, SL, sleep hours, and adherence to the diet demonstrated the highest significance. To predict the development of T2DM, a neural network (NN) classifier is proposed, which achieved remarkable accuracy (100%) during the training phase. A Levenberg-Marquardt supervised learning algorithm was employed to minimize the total error. Furthermore, Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) is leveraged to forecast glucose spike generation, enabling a comprehensive estimation over a seven-day period. The accuracy of the prediction was validated through the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), which resulted in a value of 0.5803. Clinical Relevance—This exploratory study emphasizes the importance of risk factors and preventive medicine in the context of T2DM. By shifting focus towards prevention, clinicians can transform patient care and promote better health outcomes. Leveraging the combined power of risk factor analysis and machine learning techniques empowers clinicians to effectively guide individuals at risk of developing T2DM. This approach facilitates informed lifestyle choices, potentially leading to a significant reduction in the overall disease burden. This research holds significant promise for improving population health and transforming healthcare practices towards a preventive model

articleTitle: Salud desde tu celular
abstract: Summary form only given. This document will present the idea of ​​creating, generating or launch a cell phone application, linked to a device heart signal meter like an EKG (ECG) that will monitor the rhythm and signal of the heart 24 hours a day of the person to whom it was placed, can be linked from the cell phone of the individual to whom the device was placed, another person will be able to see his signal when he requires it and always have the signal information of the person with the device placed. In emergency cases, the user will be notified, not seeing response within a defined period, you will be provided with the information to the trusted person, previously established in the application by the patient and to the emergency number. Clinical relevance - Support for patients suffering from heart problems, support for health personnel to have the patient information 24 hours a day in real time in case of a possible emergency, by this method we make it easier for the information reaches quickly and accurately to the trusted contact and emergency personnel for patient care.
